system.summary: Simple substitution: one two-digit number per letter (25 values, no homophones, no nomenclator), numbers run together without spaces, inserted into the clear sentence

prior_solution.where: Catalogue 439 open; DECODE status N/A; web search 27 Oct 2026.

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout chose the target from the catalogue and set the rules (frozen key before validation, held-out checks, prior-work search the day of publication); AI agents transcribed, solved, checked and wrote up. Doubtful signs were settled by targeted visual review where stated.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: Table rebuilt from the key sheet R7501.
Blind check: R7508 transcribed and frozen before decoding, then read with the R7501 table.
Seven letters read in Polish with English translation; R7510 redated 1663 and joined to R7509.

PR review on merge (Claude Opus 5.5 for Daniel Bourdeau): the key sheet R7501 credited; the credit for the images sent for study removed (the project is not credited in its own profiles; the thanks stay in NOTES.md).

outcome.method_basis: Key sheet R7501 in the same file, transcribed and checked blind on R7508.
outcome.fraction_read_source: R7510: 98.7% of about 700 numbers read without intervention; other letters fully valued but for a few numbers marked ‹n›.

credits.note: seven letters read with the R7501 table; Polish texts and English translations; R7510 redated

texts.label: Wąsowicz to Lubomirski, 25 January 1663 (ANK AKPot 3227, p. 200; DECODE R7505)
texts.summary: […] [to see the manoeuvres the Marshal has made.] […] [The court strives to keep the agreement with the army, and] […] diligent efforts so that [the circle of Wolbórz be satisfied.] The whole point: [that the money be brought in.] […]

texts.label: Wąsowicz to Lubomirski, 17–18 February 1663 (ANK AKPot 3227, p. 209; DECODE R7506)
texts.summary: [The Marshal] is rather well [received by Their Majesties and obtains at the audiences] […] satisfaction. […] [to the Starost of Spisz] […] [the confidence at the father’s with Bieykowski:] [he was ordered] to negotiate nothing further, only [that after the confederation he should serve the King], and that he [should watch whether the army is plotting some harm against the fatherland.] […]

texts.label: Wąsowicz to Lubomirski, 19 March 1663 (ANK AKPot 3227, p. 225; DECODE R7507)
texts.summary: […] [the Marshal] has also [sent] Tatar [prisoners?], by which he has greatly [obliged Their Majesties] here. He does not promise [to detach the better banners before the circle, but after the circle he gives assurance that a good many of them will leave the confederation. The Voivode of Ruthenia will not set out again]; the men however [will pass? under this command] […]

texts.label: Wąsowicz to Lubomirski, 5 May 1663 (ANK AKPot 3227, p. 235; DECODE R7508)
texts.summary: […] that the banner should consent to come, [in which I gave him this information], and that [in order to draw him into this obligation, so that he should attend more diligently to what he promised the lord]. But on this too I shall be able to tell Your Grace, my lord and benefactor, more.

texts.label: Wąsowicz to Lubomirski, 9 December 1663 (ANK AKPot 3227, p. 239; DECODE R7509)
texts.summary: […] for the time being the Archdeacon of Sandomierz [has not asked] in the slightest way [after Your Grace’s health.] […]

texts.label: Wąsowicz to Lubomirski, 9 December 1663, continued (Jarosław) (ANK AKPot 3227, pp. 245–248; DECODE R7510)
